proposal.billed_note: D8 (H8 dark-core backfill, audit r1 m7): this module now emits 404 proposal rows at B=6, exactly matching the paper's billed pad (n_rows == n_rows_billed == 404 on every plane). Of those 404 physical cores -- identified by the bc-flag per-vertex factorization (ref-full-basis-diff.py), validated exact against the direct B=4 enumeration (731,987 states / 81 cores) -- only 400 are ME-REALIZED: proposal_rows_measured's per-core dual-method scan finds an actual matrix-element branch for them (census_plane()['pairs'] union count agrees, test_measured_rows_400_dual_method_every_plane; that 400 figure is unaffected by this backfill -- it is still the ME-realized count, not this field's row count). The remaining 4 cores (export_tables.DARK_CORES) are PHYSICAL but matrix-element-DARK: no branch of any matrix element ever populates them, so they carry U_lambda=0 and are injected here (_plane_bundle) as empty-branch, all-reject rows (reject_weight == Uhat exactly, F-head angle == pi/2). This supersedes the prior 'sink-only tail, two independently-measured union counts diverge by 4' account, which audit r1 refuted by direct bc-flag factorization; that prior account's own record -- analysis/prep_oracle_cost.py:492-494 (DATA_VCORE[6]['stage_a']), analysis/results/familiar_prep_alternatives.md sec. 7, and prep_classical_tables.nb Step 5's pad-to-404 convention -- is left in place as history, not current provenance.
proposal.padding_rule: Two-part rule (paper_v10.tex:1244-1254). A source with fewer than the table's k=17 branches pads its unused ANGLE slots with angle zero: a zero R_y rotation is already the no-op, so it contributes no synthesis error, but it cannot be skipped, because the source register is in superposition over keys and the circuit is common to all of them. Its unused VALUE slots pad with a RESERVED WORD that no realized (lambda', DIR) encodes -- e.g. a link field value outside the active-irrep range (indices 6/7 are free in a 3-bit field) -- and NEVER the all-zero word, because the all-zero (lambda', DIR) is itself a realizable target and padding with it would make a later unused block's guarded-equality test (the W write circuit's block-flag uncompute, tex:663-670) fire on a branch that had already written a real value. This module's rows are variable-length (len(branches) angles, not padded to k=17 here); a downstream H7 consumer applies this padding rule when widening rows to the table's fixed k=17 slots.
